title: I Posted the Public-Hammock Hours After the Influencer Camped the Tree

parts.text: I unrolled at 4:22 p.m. and influencer Paz had a ring light in the only tagged oak. The sign said: ONE HAMMOCK. NINETY MINUTES. NO RIGS ON THE TAG. I was thirty-two, permit holder, holding a tag that listed the oak. Paz shrugged. "Content is the park." I photographed the sign, the tag, and the ring. Then I asked for the tree log. At 4:28 parks pinged why Paz's name was on a tagged oak overtime. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Parks can see Paz's ring light on the tagged oak during my hammock hours.

social.video_title: The influencer camped the tagged oak with a ring light — Part 1/2
social.description: Public hammock, a ninety-minute sign, a ring on the tag. I logged the tree. Would you have asked parks?

parts.text: Paz called it a reel until parks asked for the still. I printed the log, the sign, and the photo. The ring came down. Paz booked a different tree and told the next creator parks were always about optics. Optics is a word influencers use when tags exist. Hours now have a second line: RIGS ARE NOT THE OAK. I keep my ninety. Paz brown-bags the jokes. The tree finally looks like a permit, not a set. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Rigs are not the oak — Part 2/2
social.description: Tree log, ring down, and a second line on the sign. Was a reel ever my tag?
